Deterministic policy per unit:
1) Read hard constraints from payload/global/unit intent. Enforce in this order: required_action_type; required_cell/required_cells and any instruction to target/hit/end at cell X; allowed_end_cells; retreat/stay_out_of_range.
2) If required_action_type is an attack, choose an attack. Never replace a qualifying attack with move/fast_move/rest.
3) An attack qualifies when the required cell or predicted enemy landing cell is in that option's real hit coverage: target_cell, affected_cells, ray_cells, line_cells, or intercept_cells.
4) If enemy movement may occur before the hit resolves, prioritize predicted landing cells over current enemy cells. When multiple legal attacks qualify, prefer the one whose target_cell exactly equals the required/predicted landing cell; otherwise choose a target_cell whose coverage contains it. If a legal option exists, do not reject it because the target cell is friendly-occupied or because the enemy is currently elsewhere.
5) If any legal attack covers a required or predicted landing cell, choose that attack unless intent explicitly forbids attacking.
6) If no attack is chosen, obey movement constraints exactly: allowed_end_cells are mandatory; under retreat/stay_out_of_range prefer legal end cells outside enemy threat, else the safest allowed end. Only if no such constraint exists, choose move/fast_move that best reduces distance to the key enemy/objective and speeds next-turn contact.
7) Tie-break: exact hard-constraint satisfaction > exact target_cell match to required/predicted landing cell > coverage of required/predicted landing cell > attack > safer end (lower pred_damage_at_end or incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end) > shorter post-action distance > lower i.

Output rules:
- One action per AI unit.
- option_index must equal the chosen legal option's i.
- echo_cell MUST be copied exactly from the chosen option: end_cell if present, else target_cell if present, else the unit's current cell.
- Never use coverage cells or predicted landing cells as echo_cell unless that exact cell is also the chosen option's end_cell or target_cell.
- Keep both strings brief and mention only cells that appear in chosen option metadata.

suggested_snapshot_fields_to_add.why: Pre-unioned hit cells removes ambiguity about whether an attack covers a required or predicted landing cell.
Makes fast-mover aim points explicit so the planner can target landing cells deterministically.
Lets the planner rank attacks without re-deriving timing/coverage intersections.

parsed.rationale: The failures cluster into four issues: (1) the model still chose movement over attacks that satisfied intent via AOE/ray coverage; (2) it aimed at current enemy cells instead of predicted landing cells when timing made landing cells the real objective; (3) it ignored mandatory movement endpoints such as allowed_end_cells during retreat; and (4) it inferred extra illegality from friendly occupancy even when the option was already listed as legal. The revised prompt makes these rules explicit, ordered, and mandatory, with a stronger tie-break that prefers exact target_cell matches to required/predicted landing cells.
parsed.expected_fix: Marine/Scout cases should now choose legal attacks whenever coverage hits the forced or predicted landing cell, and prefer target_cell equal to that landing cell when available. Retreat cases should end only within allowed_end_cells. Friendly-occupied target tiles should still be used if the legal option exists. Echo behavior remains unchanged and compliant.

prompt_debug.system_prompt:
You are the tactical planner for a hex turn-based game. Return exactly one JSON object only:
{"opponent_prediction":"string","reasoning_summary":"string","actions":[{"unit_id":NUMBER,"option_index":NUMBER,"echo_cell":[q,r]}]}
Choose exactly one action per AI unit, using only ai_units[].legal_options[].i.

Deterministic policy per unit:
1) Enforce hard intent constraints first from payload/global intent/unit intent: required_action_type, required_cell(s), allowed_end_cells, retreat, stay_out_of_range, or instructions to target/hit/end at cell X.
2) For attacks, "hit X" is satisfied if X is anywhere in that option's real coverage: target_cell, affected_cells, ray_cells, line_cells, or intercept_cells. The option does NOT need target_cell==X.
3) If an enemy can move before your hit resolves, prefer a legal attack whose coverage contains the predicted landing cell. For AOE/ray/line, choose the target_cell that makes coverage include the landing cell. If any legal attack covers a required or predicted landing cell, do not replace it with move/fast_move/rest unless intent forbids attacking.
4) Otherwise choose: lethal attack on highest-threat enemy > highest immediate damage > any attack on highest-threat enemy.
5) If no attack is chosen, obey movement intent: retreat/stay_out_of_range/allowed_end_cells first; else move/fast_move that most reduces distance to the key enemy/objective and creates fastest next-turn contact. If fast-phase same-tile contact/passive timing matters, prefer the contact-producing fast_move.
6) Tie-break: exact intent satisfaction > landing-cell coverage > attack > safer end (lower pred_damage_at_end or incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end) > shorter post-action distance > lower i.

Output rules:
- One action per AI unit.
- option_index must equal the chosen legal option's i.
- echo_cell MUST be copied exactly from the chosen option: end_cell if present, else target_cell if present, else the unit's current cell.
- Never use affected_cells, predicted landing cells, or intended hit cells as echo_cell unless that exact cell is also the chosen option's end_cell or target_cell.
- If an attack hits X via AOE/ray/line while targeting Y, that option is valid and echo_cell is Y, not X.
- Keep both strings brief and only mention cells that appear in the chosen option metadata.
